evidence.E1: preserved – physically present, tooth count measured by X-ray CT
evidence.E2: inferred – lost, but strictly required by surviving dials (ratio is unambiguous)
evidence.E3: reconstructed – model according to current research (Freeth 2021), plausible, not proven
evidence.E4: speculative – no direct evidence, added by us or researchers; designed to suit the period

assemblies.AM-150: Middle plate, pillars, circular plate, strap

a1.function: Contrate (crown) gear at the input, at right angles to the main plane; driven by the crank

b1.function: Main drive wheel, 4 spokes, approx. 13 cm; 1 turn = 1 year; carries the cosmos gearing at the front
b1.note: Tooth count: Freeth 2006 best fit 223 (limits 223/224, CT); Karakalos 223–226, Wright 223. Irrelevant for the ratios, since b1 is the reference (1 year).

b2.function: Distributor behind b1: starts the lunar and calendar trains

b3.function: Lunar output (hollow arbor to the front, moon pointer)

d2.function: Lunar train, stage 3 (127 is prime, half of 254 sidereal months)

e5.note: CT best fit 52 (limits 50–52); like Freeth 2006 in the text, the model uses 50 = k1, otherwise the lunar anomaly would have the wrong period.

e3.function: Largest wheel at the back (Saros: 223 months); also the carrier of k1/k2 (rotation of the apsides approx. 8.88 years)

e4.function: Saros train onward to the Saros spiral

k1.function: Carries the pin of the pin-and-slot coupling
k1.note: Axis offset k1/k2 approx. 1.1 mm → produces the variable speed of the Moon (Hipparchus' lunar theory)

m3.function: Branch to the Saros train (lost, required by the Saros dial)

n2.note: Named as in the literature: n2 (15) drives p1 (Freeth 2006, Spinellis 2008).

o1.function: Games pointer (4 years), the only anticlockwise pointer
o1.note: CT best fit 60 (limits 57–61). Freeth 2006 still assigned o1 to the Callippic train; since Freeth 2008 it drives the Games dial.

ma1.function: Contrate gear of the moon phase ball (turns the half dark / half light ball, approx. 6 mm)
ma1.note: 20 teeth, tip radius 5.3 mm (Freeth 2006, Suppl. Notes 3, where it is called “q1”, fragment C).

b0.function: Mean Sun as reference for the lunar phase (difference Moon − Sun)
b0.note: 20 teeth, like the contrate gear ma1 (Freeth 2021, Suppl. S6.2.6). Sits on a tube that is linked to b1 by a bar fixed to the block on spoke D (31.8 mm from the centre).

V-51.function: Fixed central gear shared by Mercury and Venus

V-44.note: Arbor 44+34 turns in the bearing on spoke C, 25.6 mm from the centre (Freeth 2021, Suppl. S5). Module approx. 0.54.

r1.function: Venus epicycle; carries the pin for the slotted follower
r1.note: Physically preserved (fragment D, only 3 teeth missing). Its role as Venus epicycle is an interpretation (E3). Axis 27.8 mm from the centre, pin on the riveted disk 20.0 mm from the gear centre (Freeth 2021, Table S9).

Me-72.note: Arbor 72+89 sits on the flattened area of spoke A, 31.6 mm from the centre (Freeth 2021, Suppl. S5).

Me-89.function: Mercury, stage 1 (same arbor as 72; 89 = prime factor of 1513 = 17 × 89)

Me-20.note: Axis 36.0 mm from the centre, pin 14.0 mm from the gear centre (Freeth 2021, Table S9).

CP-56.function: Fixed central gear on the circular plate, shared by true Sun, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn

S-52.function: True Sun idler; also on a common arbor with Saturn 61

S-56.function: Sun epicycle (fixed in space) with pin → slotted follower produces the solar anomaly

MJ-64.function: Gear shared by Mars and Jupiter

Ma-71.function: Mars epicycle with pin (71 = prime factor of 284)

Ju-43.function: Jupiter epicycle with pin (43 = prime factor of 344)

Sa-61.function: Saturn (same arbor as 52; 61 = prime factor of 427)

Dr-49.note: Freeth 2021 themselves: no direct physical evidence

Dr-62.note: Arbor 62+64 turns in the bearing on spoke B, 27.0 mm from the centre (Freeth 2021, Suppl. S4/S6). Modules 0.486 (49/62) and 0.482 (64/48).

Dr-48.function: Dragon hand output (nodal cycle 18.6 years, retrograde)

wreck.name: Antikythera wreck (Cape Glyfadia)
wreck.text: Find spot of the mechanism. Roman-era merchant ship, sank approx. 70–60 BC. Discovered in 1900 by sponge divers from Symi, salvaged 1900/01. New excavations 2021–2025 (Swiss School of Archaeology, Ephorate of Underwater Antiquities): parts of the hull recovered.

athens-nam.name: National Archaeological Museum, Athens
athens-nam.text: All 82 fragments and several reconstructions are kept here.

rhodes.name: Rhodes
rhodes.text: Favoured by many researchers: the Games dial names the Halieia of Rhodes; Rhodes was a centre of astronomy (Hipparchus worked there, later Posidonius' school). Iversen 2017: built on Rhodes, perhaps for a client from Epirus.

epirus-dodona.name: Dodona (Epirus)
epirus-dodona.text: The Naa games of Dodona appear on the Games dial. The month names match the calendar of Epirus.

ambracia.name: Ambracia (today Arta)
ambracia.text: Corinthian colony; Epirus probably adopted the Corinthian calendar from here (Iversen 2017).

corinth.name: Corinth
corinth.text: The calendar on the Metonic spiral belongs to the Corinthian family of calendars (Freeth et al. 2008, confirmed 2017).

syracuse.name: Syracuse
syracuse.text: Home of Archimedes; named as a possible origin in 2008. Iversen 2017 argues the calendar can NOT be that of Syracuse.

pergamon.name: Pergamon
pergamon.text: Coin finds (Cousteau 1976) point to a cargo from the East.

kos.name: Kos
kos.text: Koan amphorae are very common on the wreck (2024 excavation) – a hint at a route through the eastern Aegean.

rome.name: Rome (presumed destination)
rome.text: The ship was probably carrying luxury goods (statues, glass, jewellery) to Italy/Rome.

olympia.name: Olympia
olympia.text: Olympic games – on the Games dial.

delphi.name: Delphi
delphi.text: Pythian games – on the Games dial.

isthmia.name: Isthmia
isthmia.text: Isthmian games – twice on the Games dial.

nemea.name: Nemea
nemea.text: Nemean games – twice on the Games dial.

babylon.name: Babylon
babylon.text: Origin of the cycles (Saros, Metonic cycle, planetary periods) built into the mechanism.

alexandria.name: Alexandria
alexandria.text: Scientific centre of the Hellenistic world; the calendar ring carries Egyptian month names.

timeline.label: Babylonian astronomers know the Saros cycle
timeline.text: 223 lunar months – after that, eclipses repeat. Basis of the eclipse spiral.

timeline.label: Meton of Athens
timeline.text: 19 years = 235 lunar months. Basis of the Metonic spiral.

timeline.label: Callippus refines the cycle
timeline.text: 76 years = 4 Metonic cycles minus 1 day.

timeline.label: Death of Archimedes
timeline.text: Cicero later reports on a celestial globe by Archimedes – so similar devices existed.

timeline.label: Start date of the scales
timeline.text: Saros month 1 = spring 205 BC (Carman & Evans 2014, Freeth 2014). Calendar start shortly after the new moon of 23 Aug 205 BC (Iversen 2017). This is the start date of the scales, not necessarily the year of construction.

timeline.label: Alternative calibration date
timeline.text: Voulgaris et al. 2022 propose 23 Dec 178 BC.

timeline.label: Year of construction: likely period
timeline.text: Letter forms of the inscriptions: late 3rd to early 1st century BC. Many researchers: around 150–100 BC.

timeline.label: Hipparchus (active approx. 140–120 BC)
timeline.text: Lunar theory with an epicycle – implemented mechanically in the device (pin and slot).

timeline.label: Loss of the ship
timeline.text: A ship with a luxury cargo sinks off Antikythera.

timeline.label: Sponge divers find the wreck
timeline.text: Captain Dimitrios Kontos and divers from Symi.

timeline.label: Recovery of the mechanism
timeline.text: Probably July 1901, initially unnoticed.

timeline.label: Gear wheel spotted
timeline.text: 17 May 1902: Valerios Stais notices a gear wheel in the fragment.

timeline.label: Albert Rehm: astronomical calculator
timeline.text: First interpretation as a calculating machine for the heavens.

timeline.label: Derek de Solla Price: 'Gears from the Greeks'
timeline.text: First X-ray images (with Karakalos 1971), first complete model.

timeline.label: Jacques Cousteau dives at the wreck
timeline.text: Coins from Pergamon among other finds. In the same year fragment E is identified.

timeline.label: Michael Wright: working model
timeline.text: First mechanical reconstruction including planets (Wright 2002–2006).

timeline.label: X-ray CT by the AMRP
timeline.text: Antikythera Mechanism Research Project: computed tomography + surface scans; thousands of characters become legible.

timeline.label: Nature: Moon and eclipses decoded
timeline.text: Freeth et al.: rear gearing, pin-and-slot Moon, Saros.

timeline.label: Nature: calendar and Olympiads
timeline.text: Corinthian month names, Games dial.

timeline.label: Freeth & Jones: cosmos model
timeline.text: Planetary display proposed as a model.

timeline.label: Dating to 205 BC / Return to Antikythera
timeline.text: Carman & Evans; new diving excavations start in the same year.

timeline.label: Numbers 462 and 442 read
timeline.text: Periods for Venus and Saturn in the front cover inscription.

timeline.label: Iversen: calendar from Epirus, Halieia of Rhodes
timeline.text: The question of origin is revived.

timeline.label: Budiselic et al.: hole count of the calendar ring
timeline.text: New measurement of the holes under the calendar ring.

timeline.label: UCL: complete cosmos model
timeline.text: Freeth et al. 2021 – basis of our front reconstruction.

timeline.label: Excavation programme 2021–2025
timeline.text: Swiss School of Archaeology in Greece; parts of the hull found in 2024.

timeline.label: Calendar ring: 354 holes
timeline.text: Woan & Bayley (Glasgow): lunar calendar more likely than a solar year.

timeline.label: Did the gearing jam?
timeline.text: Szigety & Arenas (preprint): with the measured manufacturing errors the gearing would often have jammed – or the measurements are distorted by corrosion.

timeline.label: Hull planks recovered
timeline.text: End of the 2021–2025 excavations: hull planks recovered. First analysis: elm and oak, wood dating to around 235 BC.

papers.gemacht: First X-ray and gamma-ray images (with C. Karakalos).
papers.ergebnis: First complete model; calendar and lunar trains identified.
papers.warum: Made the mechanism world-famous as the computer of antiquity.

papers.ergebnis: Planetary displays mechanically feasible; moon phase ball.
papers.warum: Proved it could be built with ancient means.

papers.titel: Decoding the ancient Greek astronomical calculator (Nature)
papers.gemacht: Computed tomography of all fragments and surface scans. In the supplementary material: tooth counts with uncertainties and the measured radii of all surviving gears.
papers.ergebnis: Back decoded: Saros eclipse spiral, pin-and-slot Moon, tooth counts.
papers.warum: Basis of all current models. The back of this app is built on it.

papers.gemacht: Read the inscriptions on the spirals.
papers.ergebnis: Corinthian month names and a dial for the great games.

papers.titel: On the epoch of the Antikythera mechanism
papers.gemacht: Sieved the eclipse glyphs against every possible year.
papers.ergebnis: The scale fits best with a start in spring 205 BC.
papers.warum: Moves the device to shortly after Archimedes.
papers.sicherheit: Start date of the scale, not the year of construction

papers.gemacht: Re-read the glyphs, index letters and inscriptions of the Saros spiral.
papers.ergebnis: 51 glyphs; the index letters point to text passages that group eclipses by their distance from the lunar node. Two simple arithmetical models explain the whole scheme.
papers.warum: Shows that the eclipse scheme is based on arithmetic, not on lists of observations.

papers.titel: The Calendar on the Antikythera Mechanism
papers.gemacht: Compared the month names with all known Corinthian calendars.
papers.ergebnis: The calendar fits Epirus, not Syracuse. One dial names the Halieia of Rhodes.
papers.warum: Suggests construction on Rhodes, perhaps for a client from Epirus.

papers.titel: Back Plate Inscription and eclipse scheme
papers.gemacht: New edition of the inscription next to the Saros spiral, matched against all glyphs.
papers.ergebnis: Complete table of which cell carries a lunar or solar eclipse and which index letter. Solar eclipses are sorted by the Moon’s latitude.
papers.warum: Basis of the glyphs on the Saros spiral in this app.
papers.sicherheit: high for attested cells, the rest inferred

papers.gemacht: Clockmaker Chris Budiselic measured the row of holes on new X-ray images.
papers.warum: Shows that craftsmen-researchers make real contributions.

papers.titel: A Model of the Cosmos (Scientific Reports)
papers.gemacht: Combined newly read numbers for Venus (462) and Saturn (442), traces on the main wheel and the puzzling 63-tooth gear.
papers.ergebnis: Complete front gearing with shared gears; planets as rings with gemstone markers.
papers.warum: First model that fits all the evidence. The front of this app is built on it.
papers.sicherheit: plausible, explicitly not a copy of the original

papers.gemacht: Alternative analysis of the Saros spiral.
papers.warum: Shows how uncertain the dating still is.

papers.gemacht: Applied statistics from gravitational-wave research to the hole measurements.
papers.ergebnis: 354 or 355 holes on a 77.1 mm radius. 365 is not plausible.
papers.warum: The calendar ring probably followed the lunar year.

papers.gemacht: Computer simulation with triangular teeth and measured spacing errors.
papers.ergebnis: Triangular teeth alone work. With the measured errors the gearing usually jams early.
papers.warum: Either the device was hard to operate, or corrosion distorts the measurements. No evidence for a toy.
